summary: Julius Euting was a scholar of linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tübingen, including under Rudolf von Roth and doctoral supervisor Ernst Heinrich Meier, later serving as director at the Bibliothèque nationale et universitaire and honorary professor at Strasbourg.

Julius Grill was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tübingen under doctoral supervisor Rudolf von Roth, as well as under Adalbert Kuhn and at Jena. He served as professor of Old Testament exegesis at Tübingen (1888–1913).

Julius Jolly was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied in Berlin, Leipzig, Munich, and Würzburg under Martin Haug and Albrecht Weber. He served as a lecturer and professor at the University of Würzburg and Tagore Professor at Calcutta.

Julius Lipner worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Jnana-Deepa Vidyapeeth, Jadavpur University, and King's College London under doctoral supervisor Hywel David Lewis. He later became Professor of Hinduism and the Comparative Study of Religion at Cambridge.

Julius Mohl was an Iranian, Central Asian, and Sinology scholar. He studied at Tübingen and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat, and Eugène Burnouf. He held professorships at the University of Tübingen and the Collège de France (1847–1876).

Julius Müller was a religious studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at the universities of Breslau, Göttingen, and Berlin. He later held posts at the universities of Göttingen (~1831–1834), Marburg (~1835–1839), and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1839–1878).

Julius Pokorny worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Vienna under Rudolf Much. He held academic posts at Vienna (~1913–1920), Humboldt University of Berlin (~1920–1935), and later at Bern (~1944–1953) and Zurich (~1944–1959).
Julius Schubring studied at the University of Göttingen (~1857–1859), the University of Bonn (~1859–1860), and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1860–1862).
Jun Fujii is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He served as a full-time lecturer at Komazawa University from around 2009 to 2013.

Jun Takashima is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara. He held posts at Aichi Prefectural University (~1993–1998) and served as a professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies in 2020.

Jun Yang works in linguistics, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, Yang held posts as Senior Lecturer in Chinese Language at the University of Chicago and as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University.

Jundo Nagashima works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from the University of Bristol under Paul Williams, and also studied under Seitatsu Matsunami and Alexis Sanderson. He served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 2013–2017).

June McDaniel is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned an MTS at Emory University and a PhD at the University of Chicago. She served as Professor of the History of Religions at the College of Charleston (attested 2015).

Junglan Bang is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at Dongguk University and the University of Hamburg (PhD 2012) under Harunaga Isaacson, Seung-suk Jung, and Sungdoo Ahn, and served as a visiting researcher at Kyoto University.

Jungmin Ha is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Ha studied under Juhyung Rhi at Seoul National University and completed a PhD at Duke University under Stanley Abe (attested 2016).

Junjirō Takakusu was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Oxford, Leipzig, and Tokyo under Friedrich Max Müller, Sylvain Lévi, and Moriz Winternitz. He was professor and president at the University of Tokyo and headed multiple other institutions.

Junkei Washio was a Buddhist studies and history and archaeology scholar. He studied at Toyo University and later served as a professor at Toyo University (~1904–1935) and Komazawa University, while also holding a post at Sendan-Rin School.

Junkichi Imanishi is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Ernst Waldschmidt. He served as associate professor at Hokkaido University, chancellor of the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and director of IIBS.

Junko Matsumura is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed an MA at the Australian National University (1980) and doctoral work at the University of Göttingen (1990). Matsumura served as a professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2011).

Junko Minamoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed coursework at Ryukoku University and Otani University. Minamoto held a post as a commissioned researcher at Kansai University.
